correctness.rationale: The five degree-four monomial orbit sums span precisely the cyclic invariants. The weighted coordinate change w→w+(x+y+z)² toggles the coefficients of A+B+C+E, and exchanging coordinates swaps B with C. Smoothness forces a singular point onto the nonsingular branch conic; substitution of its homogeneous parametrization reduces all geometric singularities, not just rational singularities, to endpoint checks and gcds of explicit F2[t] polynomials, yielding exactly 12 masks. The 12 masks split into four classes after the shift and coordinate symmetry; the four distinct Frobenius polynomials exclude any further F2-isomorphism. The known rank-eight geometric Picard representation of smooth degree-two del Pezzo surfaces and the Grothendieck trace formula convert exactly counted points over F_{2^n} for n=1,...,8 via Newton identities to the full characteristic polynomial and all extension counts. Independent computation rederived all 12 smooth masks, all four normalized classes and Picard traces for n=1,...,8 using an independent finite-field evaluator. None of this finite work by itself proves the geometric rank-eight theorem; that is a named standard input.

value.rationale: The complete cyclic-invariant coefficient space with fixed smooth conic is a natural finite moduli slice, not a freely chosen short list of examples. The exact smooth-locus and geometric isomorphism classification, including two equal-rational-point pairs distinguished by arithmetic Picard rank, is a meaningful arithmetic-geometric classification. It is neither claimed as a classification of all degree-two del Pezzo surfaces nor as a new general inverse-Galois theorem.

final_claim: In the 32 cyclic-invariant weighted double-plane models w²+(xy+xz+yz)w+f4=0 over F2, exactly 12 are geometrically smooth and these form four F2-isomorphism types, with four explicitly determined degree-eight geometric Picard Frobenius characteristic polynomials.
limitations: Only the cyclic invariant 32-model family over F2 with fixed q=xy+xz+yz is classified; not all characteristic-two degree-two del Pezzo surfaces.
